solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Pounds exchanged for hotel in good-humoured game (8)

indicatorNotes.exchanged for: one letter is traded away and another taken in its place

blocks.note: pleasant = good-humoured
L = pounds (librae), the letter taken out
H = hotel in the NATO alphabet, the letter put in

annotation.surface: Someone swaps sterling for a hotel stay as part of a cheerful game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Game' reads as a pastime, but here it is birds shot for sport.
annotation.definitionFit: Game here means birds hunted for sport, and the pheasant is the most familiar example.

entries.clue: Obscure by the sound of it, this writer’s best-selling novel (5)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: tells you to take a word as it is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: to obscure is to hide; the first four letters are spelt differently but sound like that word
this writer = the setter = I; the ’s means 'is'

annotation.surface: An author boasts that their best-seller has been unjustly overlooked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This writer’s' is I plus 'is', not a possessive. Heidi is Johanna Spyri's Swiss children's novel, one of the best-selling books ever.
annotation.definitionFit: Heidi has sold tens of millions of copies worldwide.

entries.clue: Take out two mugs during fancy tea (11)

indicatorNotes.fancy: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or rearranged

blocks.note: a mug is a fool, an ass; two of them
in = during
TEA rearranged

annotation.surface: An invitation to bring two cups along to an elegant tea party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take out' and 'mugs' both sound like a café order; here they mean kill and fools.
annotation.definitionFit: To take someone out is slang for killing them.

entries.clue: Periodical article in reverse (6)

blocks.note: to reverse a decision is to annul it
a = the indefinite article, placed before the final L

annotation.surface: A magazine piece printed back to front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In reverse' looks like a reversal instruction, but 'in' is the container and 'reverse' means cancel.
annotation.definitionFit: An annual is a publication issued once a year.

entries.clue: Propose returning money in place of fare? (8)

indicatorNotes.returning: going back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: in British usage, to table a motion is to put it forward
a pot is a pool of money, as in poker

annotation.surface: Suggesting that cash be handed back instead of a paid journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a bus ticket; here it is food, which sits on a tabletop.
annotation.definitionFit: Fare is food, and a tabletop is where the meal is laid.

entries.clue: Count in German back from hundert — it’s hard work (5)

indicatorNotes.back from: the back of the word, its final letter

blocks.note: Graf is the German title for a count
the last letter of the German word for hundred

annotation.surface: Counting down from a hundred in German is a laborious chore.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb about numbers; it is the nobleman. Graft is British slang for hard work.
annotation.definitionFit: In British English graft means hard, sustained work.

entries.clue: Shut up — something comedian should do (3)

blocks.note: to silence someone by stopping their mouth with a cloth
a comedian's job is to crack jokes, and the same word names a joke

annotation.surface: A heckler tells a comic to be quiet, which is the opposite of their job.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses pull against each other: one silences, the other makes people laugh.
annotation.definitionFit: Gag means both to silence and to crack jokes.

entries.clue: Terrified when lorry clips our side (9)

indicatorNotes.clips: to clip is to fasten round, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: as = when
lorry is the British word for a truck
we = our side, us

annotation.surface: A driver is shaken after a lorry grazes their side of the car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clips' suggests the lorry striking a glancing blow; here it means holds, as a paper clip holds sheets.
annotation.definitionFit: Awestruck can mean filled with dread as well as wonder.

entries.clue: Essay about old enemy of Starmer, perhaps (4)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the attempt is wrapped around old

blocks.note: an essay is an attempt, a try
O = old, the common abbreviation

annotation.surface: A piece of writing on a former opponent of the Labour leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a school composition; it is the older sense of an attempt. Keir Starmer leads the Labour Party, whose main rivals are the Conservatives, or Tories.
annotation.definitionFit: A Tory is a Conservative, the traditional opponent of Labour's Starmer.

entries.clue: Thrill small boy on last day of school? (7)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, A on B means A comes after B, so small boy is sent second

blocks.note: Friday is the last day of the school week
S = small, as on clothing labels
a son is a boy

annotation.surface: A child's excitement as the school holidays arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: The '?' flags that 'last day of school' means the week, not the end of term.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, borrowed from French: a shiver of excitement.

entries.clue: Because bed’s missing odd pieces, have a go at woodwork? (8)

indicatorNotes.missing odd pieces: drop the 1st, 3rd and other odd-numbered letters, keeping the even ones

blocks.note: for = because
the even letters of BEDS
to try is to have a go

annotation.surface: A broken bed prompts someone to try carpentry.
annotation.walkthrough: Woodwork suggests carpentry; the '?' flags work in the woods instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Forestry is the tending of woodland, literally work with woods.

entries.clue: Get to tolerate particular pain (7)

blocks.note: to get to someone is to annoy them, to bug them
bear = tolerate

annotation.surface: Advice on learning to put up with a specific ache.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get to' reads as 'manage to'; it means irritate.
annotation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of annoyance, a pet hate.

entries.clue: Check gallery staff in street return to office (13)

blocks.note: to rein in is to check
St = street
the Tate, the London art gallery
staff = men, the workforce

annotation.surface: Museum employees are made to go back to their desks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Check' reads as an inspection of the staff; it means restrain, as reins do a horse. The Tate is a London art gallery.
annotation.definitionFit: Reinstatement is being restored to a former post.

entries.clue: Structure likely to induce vertigo, for we feel it wobbles (6,5)

indicatorNotes.wobbles: the letters shake into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Visitors high up a tall tower feel dizzy as it seems to sway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' does double duty: it is fodder and also reads as 'because' in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: The Eiffel Tower is a 330-metre structure whose heights make visitors dizzy.

entries.clue: Warmth under your covers accompanied by loud blasts (8)

indicatorNotes.covers: the surrounding words cover the answer, which lies inside them

blocks.note: inside warmTH UNDER Your

annotation.surface: Snug under the duvet while a storm rages outside.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures cosy bedclothes; 'covers' is the instruction to look inside the words.
annotation.definitionFit: Thundery weather comes with loud claps of thunder.

entries.clue: Time absent, that is accompanied by criticism? (6)

annotation.definition: Time absent, that is accompanied by criticism?

indicatorNotes.absent: absent means not present, so time is missing from the word

blocks.note: to give someone stick is to criticise them
T = time, removed from STICK
i.e. = that is

annotation.surface: Taking a day off draws disapproval from colleagues.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a sickie is time off that invites criticism. SICKIE is British slang for a day off claimed as illness when not ill.
annotation.definitionFit: A sickie is a day off work pretending to be ill, which invites stick.

entries.clue: Notice aliens during approach shot military training post (9)

indicatorNotes.during: the pieces happen within another, so they sit inside it

blocks.note: in golf a chip is a short approach shot to the green
an ad is a notice
ETs = extraterrestrials

annotation.surface: A notice about aliens appears during golf at an army base.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' sits beside 'military' to suggest gunfire; the chip is a golf stroke, a short lofted one onto the green.
annotation.definitionFit: A cadetship is a trainee's place in the armed forces.

entries.clue: Uncomfortable feeling toilet water connected to wrong pipe? (3,5)

annotation.definition2: toilet water connected to wrong pipe?

blocks.note: a sudden spell of feeling overheated, common in menopause

blocks.clueFragment: toilet water connected to wrong pipe?
blocks.note: a cryptic picture: a cistern plumbed by mistake into the heated supply

annotation.surface: A plumbing mistake leaves the loo running with hot water.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic picture, flagged by the '?': a flush from the hot pipe.
annotation.definitionFit: A hot flush is a sudden, uncomfortable surge of heat, as in menopause.

entries.clue: Female colonial bishop supports imam she converted (8)

indicatorNotes.supports: in a down answer, the piece that supports sits underneath

blocks.note: IMAM SHE rearranged
anagram indicator
B = bishop in chess notation

annotation.surface: A bishop backs a woman imam who has changed faith.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Converted' suggests religious conversion, fitting the bishop and imam; it means rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Memsahib was the term for a European woman in colonial India.

entries.clue: Angry-looking US agent ran after Spooner (3-5)

indicatorNotes.after Spooner: swap the opening sounds, as Rev. Spooner did

blocks.note: a Fed is an FBI agent
raced = ran
swap F and R

annotation.surface: An FBI man sprints in pursuit of a clergyman named Spooner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' reads as chasing; it means 'in the manner of'.
annotation.definitionFit: Anger flushes the face, so red-faced describes an angry look.

entries.clue: Yank wearing old jacket (6)

blocks.note: to yank is to jerk
in = wearing, as in 'in a coat'

annotation.surface: An American dressed in a vintage coat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American; it is the verb pull.
annotation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket of former times.

entries.clue: A horde’s descriptor primarily is wandering (6)

annotation.definitionNote: droves is plural in form but names one great crowd

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means in the first place, so descriptor gives its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of descriptor
roves = is wandering

annotation.surface: A remark that a mob's defining trait is that it roams.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as a possessive but means 'is'. 'In droves' means in great crowds.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: droves are great moving crowds, a horde.

entries.clue: Certain charges to deal with over shifting wealth (8,5)

indicatorNotes.charges: one piece loads or fills another
indicatorNotes.shifting: the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: sure = certain
to treat is to deal with
OVER rearranged

annotation.surface: Some fees payable on the transfer of assets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like fees; it means loads or fills, as a gun is charged.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a found hoard of valuables is one kind of wealth.

entries.clue: Current beneath duck shown presumably running smoothly (5)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down answer, beneath puts current below duck

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket
I = electric current in physics
led = shown, as in shown the way

annotation.surface: A stream flowing under a duck, which glides along.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' hedges: an oiled machine should run smoothly.
annotation.definitionFit: Something oiled has been lubricated so it will run smoothly.

entries.clue: Deliberate heat with spices (4)

blocks.note: to deliberate is to ponder, turn something over
warming wine or cider with spices, as at Christmas

annotation.surface: Intentionally warm something with seasoning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' reads as an adjective; it is the verb meaning ponder.
annotation.definitionFit: To mull is both to ponder and to spice and warm a drink.

entries.clue: Remove fastening from unopened box full of clobber (7)

indicatorNotes.unopened: unopened means not opened up, so the word's opening letter is gone

blocks.note: to box is to punch; PUNCH without its P
to clobber is to hit

annotation.surface: Taking the clasp off a sealed crate stuffed with clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: Box and clobber look like nouns (clobber is British slang for gear); both are verbs for striking.
annotation.definitionFit: To unhitch is to unfasten something tied or hooked on.

entries.clue: Great deal on those tops excluding stockings (3)

indicatorNotes.excluding: excluding means leaving out, so the stockings are left out of those
indicatorNotes.tops: in a down answer, the piece that tops sits above

blocks.note: a deletion: THOSE minus HOSE leaves T
hose = stockings, the removed letters
on as written

annotation.surface: A bargain on underwear that doesn't include hosiery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tops' looks like garments beside the stockings; it places T above ON.
annotation.definitionFit: A ton is informal for a great deal, as in 'tons of time'.

entries.clue: Like audio but not rhythm? Promise TV won’t show tango (7)

blocks.note: a vow is a promise
telly is British slang for TV
T = tango in the NATO alphabet, removed from TELLY

annotation.surface: A sound engineer promises the broadcast will play without any dance music.
annotation.walkthrough: AUDIO is four vowels in five letters and RHYTHM has none; the definition is about spelling, not sound.
annotation.definitionFit: Audio is full of vowels and rhythm has none, so only audio is vowelly.

entries.clue: Pretty spiky plant left out of bed then included (5)

blocks.note: L = left
up = out of bed
in means included, as in 'count me in'

annotation.surface: A thorny garden plant is dug out of a flower bed and later replanted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spiky' suggests thorns; lupins grow their flowers on tall spikes.
annotation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower borne on tall, showy spikes.

entries.clue: Mount top quality horse? (8)

blocks.note: best = top quality
a horse is a ride, something you ride

annotation.surface: A question about climbing onto a first-class horse.
annotation.walkthrough: The '?' admits that a horse is only one example of a ride.
annotation.definitionFit: To bestride a horse is to sit astride it, to mount it.
